title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is preparing the auxiliary quantities needed to compute lunar eclipses: the apparent semidiameters, the horizontal parallaxes and the true hourly motions of the Sun and Moon. The page finishes the solar part and does the lunar distance part.

(1) The opening sentence closes §1–3 from the previous page. Given the Sun's eccentric anomaly V, the solar diameter, the solar parallax and the true hourly motion can now be tabulated.

(2) §4, the Moon.
- Let c be the mean Earth–Moon distance (100000) and z the true distance.
- Apparent diameter = (c/z)·31'13½''. A marginal note corrects this to 31'14½''.
- Horizontal parallax = (c/z)·56'39''.
- Euler notes the simplest route is to compute z itself. Alternatively one can expand c/z as a trigonometric series directly.
- He writes the distance series (computed earlier in the work) with literal coefficients:
  z/c = 1 + k cos v − a cos V + b cos(v+V) − c cos(v−V) + d cos η − e cos 2η − f cos(2η−2v) − g cos(2η+v) + h cos(2η−v) + j cos(2η+V) + k' cos(2η−V) − l cos(2η−v+V) − m cos(2η−v−V).
- Here v is the Moon's anomaly. It is probably the eccentric anomaly, since the previous page treats the Sun by y = a(1 + e cos V) with V the eccentric anomaly; then 1 + k cos v is the exact ellipse with no cos 2v term. V is the Sun's anomaly and η is the elongation of Moon from Sun.
- The arguments correspond to known inequalities:
  - cos η: parallactic inequality;
  - cos 2η: variation;
  - cos(2η−v): evection;
  - cos V: annual equation;
  - the remaining terms: combination terms.

(3) §5. The coefficients are given as 10-figure-style logarithms (characteristic +10). For example k = 0.05444, h = 0.010216, e = 0.006983.
- c/z is then obtained by inverting 1 + X, i.e. 1 − X + X² − X³, keeping products up to second order (k³ terms for the pure eccentricity part).
- The product-to-sum contributions are arranged in columns under each argument. Examples:
  - constant: 1 + ½k² + ½h²;
  - cos v: −k − ¾k³ − e·h − f·h;
  - cos 2η: e − kg + kh;
  - cos(2η−2v): f + kh;
  - cos(2η+v): g − ke;
  - cos(2η−v): −h − ke − kf;
  - similar entries for the solar-anomaly cross terms.

(4) §6 starts the numerical result: c/z = 1.00160 − 0.05464 cos v + 0.00148 cos 2v + 0.00012 cos V + … , with logs underneath. It continues on the next page.
- Multiplying by 31'13½'' and 56'39'' gives the lunar diameter and parallax series of p. 386.
- That gives parallax ≈ 56'44'' − 186 cos v + 5 cos 2v − cos η + 25 cos 2η + 2 cos(2η−2v) − 36 cos(2η−v).

Verification of the coefficients:
- cos v: k + ¾k³ + eh + fh = 0.05444 + 0.00012 + 0.00007 + 0.000002 = 0.05464. Exact.
- cos 2η: 0.006983 − 0.000021 + 0.000556 = 0.007519, against Euler's 0.00752. Agrees.
- cos(2η−2v): 0.000204 + 0.000556 = 0.000760. Agrees.
- cos(2η−v): 0.010216 + 0.000380 + 0.000011 = 0.010607, against Euler's 0.01061. Agrees.
- cos(2η−v±V): match to the last digit.
- cos(2η+v): g − ke = 0.000378 − 0.000380 ≈ 0. This explains why the cos(2η+v) term silently disappears from the final series on the next page. It is a genuine cancellation, not an omission.
errors: Constant term: from the formulas written, 1 + ½k² + ½h² = 1.00153 (1.00156 if the omitted ½e² and the cubic −X³ cross term 1.5·k·h·e are included). Euler prints 1.00160 (log 0.00069). The discrepancy is about 4–7·10⁻⁵, i.e. under 0.3'' in parallax, so it is negligible in effect.

cos V coefficient: a + kb − kc − hl − hm = 1.4388e-4 + 0.95e-5 − 1.04e-5 − 0.19e-5 − 0.11e-5 ≈ 1.40e-4. Euler prints 0.00012 (log 6.07918, i.e. 1.200e-4). This looks like an arithmetic slip of about 2e-5, worth roughly 0.04'' in diameter, so negligible.
On the next page both the cos(v+V) and cos(v−V) coefficients receive the identical log 6.25527 (1.800e-4). Recomputation gives about 1.81e-4 and 1.85e-4. This is minor rounding or copying.
The second-order truncation is inconsistent: only some squared terms enter the constant (½k², ½h², but not ½e²). This is immaterial at the stated precision of 1–2''.
The marginal note corrects the mean lunar diameter from 31'13½'' to 31'14½''. It is not propagated into the next page's 31'17''.

ideas.what: Inversion of a lunar radius-vector trigonometric series to obtain c/z (proportional to parallax and apparent diameter) by binomial expansion and product-to-sum bookkeeping
ideas.modern_name: Lunar parallax series / Poisson-series inversion of 1/r
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century practice (Euler, Mayer, Clairaut, d'Alembert); later systematized by Laplace, Delaunay and Brown (Brown's parallax series)
ideas.where_published: Euler's Theoria motuum lunae (1772, E418) and its tables give distance and parallax; this posthumous fragment (E838, Opera postuma II, 1862)

ideas.what: Apparent diameter and horizontal parallax of the Moon taken proportional to c/z with fixed mean values (31'13½'', 56'39'')
ideas.modern_name: Lunar semidiameter–parallax proportionality (constant ratio ≈ 0.2725 × parallax for the semidiameter)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Ptolemy onward in principle; quantitatively Mayer and Euler era)
ideas.where_published: Euler's lunar tables / Theoria motuum lunae (1772)

ideas.what: Cancellation of the cos(2η+v) term in c/z: g − k·e ≈ 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in all lunar parallax theories; modern value about 3'' in parallax arising from a mean-anomaly formulation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine numerical conversion of Euler's lunar distance series into parallax and diameter series for eclipse computation. The arithmetic is correct to within small slips, and the method and results are standard for 18th-century lunar theory and already published in Euler's lunar work. The only mildly interesting detail is the near-exact cancellation of the cos(2η+v) term, which explains its silent omission on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The line beginning 'Ad quodvis igitur tempus' is partly obscured by the dark binding shadow in the scan; the reading is plausible.
In the §5 expansion, the second entry under cos(v−V) should be read as fraktur k·h (+𝔨𝔥, from 𝔨cos(2η−V)·𝔥cos(2η−v)). The glyph resembles 𝔟𝔥, but the product-to-sum calculation confirms 𝔨𝔥.
The column layout of the §5 expansion: constant column holds +½kk and +½𝔥𝔥; cos v column holds −𝔢𝔥, −𝔣𝔥 and −¾k³. The transcription's assignment is consistent with this and with the arithmetic.
The anomaly symbol is printed as v on this page and as ϱ on the next page's transcription. These are the same variable, the Moon's anomaly.
The logarithm 7,8437310 for 𝔢 shows a damaged final digit in the scan (0 vs 6). The value 7,8437310 is consistent with Euler's cos 2η result.
